solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Summary of a British Standard pamphlet

parts.note: BS is the abbreviation for British Standard, the UK national standards mark
a tract is a short pamphlet, often religious or political

explanation.surface: Someone wants the executive summary of an official standards leaflet.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstract is a short précis placed at the head of a paper or report.

clue.text: Little nail holding one decorative band

indicators.note: the small nail holds, or contains, the letter for one inside it

parts.note: a brad is a small thin nail with a tiny head
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A tiny tack is used to pin a single ornamental strip in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Braid is woven trimming sewn onto uniforms and curtains as ornament.

clue.text: A number are inclined not to finish

indicators.note: not allowed to finish means the word for are inclined loses its final letter

parts.note: to tend to do something is to be inclined to do it

explanation.surface: A crowd of people tend to give up before the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten is a particular integer, so it is one example of a number.

clue.text: A bit separate

parts.note: a part is a bit or portion of something

explanation.surface: Something is described as slightly detached from the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Things set apart are kept at a distance from each other, divided.

clue.text: Communist cause overturned on demand

indicators.note: in a down clue, overturned means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: Red is the traditional label for a communist
the root of something is its cause or origin

explanation.surface: A communist movement sees its cause defeated just when it was demanded.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods made to order are produced when a customer requests them, as needed.

clue.text: Make fun of Alice's turtle?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ridicule or tease
second meaning: the ... Turtle in Lewis Carroll's Alice in Wonderland, so the word is the turtle's first name; the question mark flags the indirect sense

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses share one word: the verb for ridicule and the adjective attached to the sad turtle Alice meets.
explanation.definitionFit: To mock is to taunt or deride, and Carroll's character is called the Mock Turtle.

clue.text: Maybe prelate's morning so organised

indicators.note: organised means the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A senior churchman's morning is arranged for him in detail.
explanation.definitionFit: Monsignor is an honorific title given to certain Catholic clergy, such as a prelate, so a prelate is one example.

clue.text: Wild romance in Italian city

indicators.note: wild means the letters run riot into a different order

explanation.surface: A passionate love affair takes place in a city in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Cremona is a town in Lombardy famous for violin makers like Stradivari.

clue.text: Pub next to new outbuilding

parts.note: a bar is a pub or the counter in one

explanation.surface: A shed stands beside the village inn.
explanation.definitionFit: A barn is a farm structure separate from the house, used for storing crops or animals.

clue.text: Came to a big hill, extremely exhausted

parts.note: a mount is a mountain or large hill

indicators.note: extremely means take only the extremes, the outer letters, of the next word

parts.note: first and last letters of exhausted

explanation.surface: A walker reached a big hill completely worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Came to' looks like regaining consciousness, but it means totalled.
explanation.definitionFit: If a bill amounted to a sum, it totalled or added up to that figure.

clue.text: Sort of guess a graduate might make?

definitions.text: Sort of guess a graduate might make?

parts.words: Sort of guess a graduate might make?
parts.note: an informed guess has a standard name; since a graduate has been to university, any guess they make is literally one from a schooled person

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for an informed guess is reread literally: a graduate is someone who has had schooling, so their guess qualifies.
explanation.definitionFit: A graduate is schooled and learned, which is exactly what the adjective in the phrase for an informed guess means.

clue.text: Angry about mixed styles of music

parts.note: cross means angry or annoyed
over can mean about, as in arguing over something

explanation.surface: Someone is furious about genres of music being blended together.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossover music fuses genres, such as classical performers singing pop.

clue.text: In India, study religious image

parts.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: In India a visitor examines a sacred picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a painted panel of a holy figure, venerated in Orthodox churches.

clue.text: Very unconventional means of escape

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an informal adjective for bizarre or far from normal
second meaning: an exit, as on a sign

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a strange escape plan, but the two parts are separate senses of one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for weird and also the label above an exit door.

clue.text: Happen to be employing? That's funny

parts.note: am is the first-person present of be, as in I happen to be (am) here
using means employing

explanation.surface: Someone admits to using something, and another person finds it comical.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amusing is entertaining and makes people laugh; the def is an exclamation-style adjective phrase.

clue.text: Little monkey, almost tame, ran freely round one

indicators.note: almost means the word tame falls short by its final letter
round means the rearranged letters go around the letter for one
freely means the letters of ran are allowed to move around

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A small monkey, nearly domesticated, ran about loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost tame' is wordplay, not description: the monkey is named by the last word of 'Little monkey'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamarins are small South American primates related to marmosets.

clue.text: Learnt to change regular payment

indicators.note: to change means the letters are altered into another order

explanation.surface: Someone learnt to switch how they make a recurring payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A rental is the fee paid periodically to hire property or equipment.

clue.text: Men's general appearance remarked on

indicators.note: remarked on means spoken, so we hear the word rather than see it

parts.note: guise means outward appearance or semblance

explanation.surface: Someone comments on how the men look overall.
explanation.definitionFit: Guys is informal for males or fellows.

clue.text: Make effort to remember note by rebel

parts.note: a memo is a short written note
to rise up is to rebel against authority

explanation.surface: Someone writes a note so they will recall a rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: To memorise is to learn something by heart so it stays in the mind.

clue.text: A lady looking up and down

indicators.note: in a down clue the word reads the same whether you look up or down, a palindrome

parts.note: a polite title for a woman, and its letters read the same in both directions

explanation.surface: A woman is eyeing someone from head to toe.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface describes a woman's scrutiny; the indicator instead means the letters read identically both ways down the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Madam is a polite form of address for a woman, used like ma'am.

clue.text: Scratch all points earned

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ... a surface is to scratch or cut a line in it
second meaning: the total tally in a game

explanation.walkthrough: The two parts are separate senses: a verb for marking a surface and a noun for a tally.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is a match total, and to score glass is to cut a groove in it.

clue.text: Made to reflect, perhaps, delivers broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone made to think things over delivers a radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflect' suggests thinking, but it means shine back light, as a mirror backed with silver does.
explanation.definitionFit: Mirrors are silvered, coated with metal to make them shine back an image; 'perhaps' marks this as one example.

clue.text: Infantry base

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... soldiers collectively, as in the ... regiments
second meaning: the bottom of something

explanation.walkthrough: Military context suggests an army base, but base here is simply the bottom of something.
explanation.definitionFit: British regiments of soldiers who march are called the Foot, and the lowest point of a page is its foot.

clue.text: At first find computer technology appropriate

indicators.note: at first means use only the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: first letter of find
IT is information technology, computing

explanation.surface: Initially someone finds the computer equipment suitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Fit as an adjective means suitable or proper, as in fit for purpose.

clue.text: Russian, somewhat vigorous

indicators.note: somewhat means only some of the word vigorous is used, the letters inside it

explanation.surface: A man from Russia is described as fairly energetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Igor is a common male first name in Russia, so it stands for a Russian man.

clue.text: It's unimportant, but not more dull?

parts.note: no can mean not, as in no better
matt means dull, without shine, so matter is more dull

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs that it doesn't matter, though it could hardly be more boring.
explanation.walkthrough: MATTER is read as the comparative of matt, a dull finish of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying no matter dismisses something as irrelevant or of no consequence.
